subject: Availability commitments & maintenance cadence — finalizing SLA language
messages:
From: Maria Cruz <maria.cruz@stellarpay.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stellarpay.com>, ops@stellarpay.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Availability commitments + maintenance cadence — draft SLA

Hi Hannah and Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is the SLA excerpt our procurement team drafted from the last call (StellarPay_SLA_Proposed_20280720.pdf). High level asks from our side:

- Uptime target: 99.95% monthly for the production inference endpoint used for transaction scoring.
- Service credits: Sliding scale starting at 5% monthly credit for <99.95 and up to 25% if availability drops below 99.0%.
- Response times: Severity 1 (production outage) — initial response within 1 hour, remediation SLA of 8 hours for critical incidents.
- Maintenance windows: Allow up to 8 hours/month of scheduled maintenance with a 72-hour advance notice; no more than two consecutive maintenance windows affecting production.

A couple of quick asks from ops: can you confirm whether dedicated capacity would be committed or if you rely on shared pools for our expected Q4 throughput? Also want to flag that StellarPay requires audit logs for all admin activity.

Can you push back with any non-starters? If possible we’d like to get language we can pass to legal by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Maria Cruz
Head of Infrastructure Operations
StellarPay

--
Attachment: StellarPay_SLA_Proposed_20280720.pdf (pdf, 142 KB)

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Cruz <maria.cruz@stellarpay.com>, Procurement <procurement@stellarpay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability commitments + maintenance cadence — draft SLA

Hi Maria — appreciate the clear summary and the draft. Quick reactions below and then I’ll loop in Legal for tracked edits.

1) Uptime target: 99.95% monthly is reasonable for a dedicated pool. For shared pools we can commit to 99.9% and offer 99.95% if you opt for a dedicated reserved capacity plan (we can model credits/pricing).

2) Service credits: the sliding scale is fine but we typically cap credits at 15% for availability breaches to avoid open-ended cost exposure. If StellarPay needs a higher cap we can discuss in commercial terms tied to a higher reservation level.

3) Response times: initial response within 1 hour for Sev1 is doable for our Enterprise SLA with on-call rotation. Remediation SLA of 8 hours — Legal flags that guaranteed remediation timing for complex incidents (third-party infra, region outages) is risky. Suggest: target remediation times with objective-based credits, not absolute cure requirements.

4) Maintenance windows: 8 hours/month + 72-hour notice is OK, but we need a clause for emergency maintenance (security patches) with shorter notice and an outage-mitigation plan. Also propose a blackout period during StellarPay month-end close windows — can you share the dates?

I’m attaching a short summary of what I’ll ask Legal to redline. Looping in Neha to capture the specific language changes and Rishi for any ops constraints on dedicated capacity.

Thanks — Hannah
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability commitments + maintenance cadence — draft SLA (tracked redlines attached)

Team — attaching the tracked redline (redlines_track_StellarPay.docx) and summarizing key legal positions so we can converge before passing back to StellarPay legal: 

- Availability metric: Accept 99.95% for dedicated pool only. For shared pool, counter with 99.9%. Proposed clause: "Availability commitments apply only to covered services running on reserved/dedicated capacity as specified in the Order Form."

- Credits cap: Propose a maximum aggregate credit cap of 15% of monthly recurring charges. If customer requests higher, escalate to Sales for commercial uplift.

- Remediation vs response: Replace guaranteed remediation times with service-level objectives for remediation and define "Initial Response" and "Remediation Effort" separately. Example: "Initial Response" = acknowledge and begin triage within 1 hour; "Remediation Effort" = use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate within a timeline based on incident classification.

- Emergency maintenance: Add explicit carve-out for "Emergency Security Maintenance" with immediate-when-required notice and a requirement to provide post-event incident report and credits only if negligence is demonstrated.

- Audit logs & admin access: We can provide admin activity logs for a 12-month retention period; additional retention or SIEM integration can be added as a paid add-on. Need to confirm data residency requirements.

Please review the redline and flag any product/ops constraints. Dev/Rishi — I left two comments on the capacity language (lines 78-84) about how we define "reserved" and the scaling guarantee.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Availability commitments + maintenance cadence — final pass before legal

Hi Maria — thanks for the draft and for being flexible. Per Neha's redline (attached), here’s our commercial proposal to close the loop quickly:

- We will commit to 99.95% monthly availability for a dedicated reserved capacity Order Form — I'll include the pricing uplift in the updated order form.
- Credits will be capped at 15% of MRR. If StellarPay requires a higher cap, we can offer a 20% cap tied to a 12-month committed spend (we can run numbers).
- For Sev1 incidents we commit to initial response within 1 hour. Remediation will be governed by SLO language; we will provide incident reports and root cause analysis for any Sev1 event.
- Maintenance: standard scheduled maintenance up to 8 hours/month with 72-hour notice. Emergency security maintenance may be performed with as much notice as feasible; we will provide post-event reports and mitigation steps.

Next steps: Laura will update the Order Form and attach the revised Order Form + tracked SLA in DocuSign. Maria — can Procurement confirm StellarPay's month-end blackout dates and whether they want a dedicated pool from Day 1? If yes, I’ll send a DocuSign envelope with the updated order form and SLA.

Proposed DocuSign link (draft): https://www.docusign.com/recipient/ABC-123-DocuSignLink
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/5200/deal/SPD-4872

If we get confirmation on blackout dates and capacity preference today, we can send the DocuSign by EOD and aim to finalize PO terms by next week.

Best,
Laura Bennett
